method: The probe measured the actual public Workspace::files API. The original library source was read from the recorded Git revision, installed temporarily in this isolated worktree for the baseline run, and restored in a finally block before measuring the candidate. Both variants used the same probe and equivalent synthetic fixtures; each sample checked the complete sorted path list against generated fixture names, and fixture names were checked against the initial hash manifest.

negative_control.method: A cfg(test) thread-local byte counter immediately after the actual regular-file read records bytes returned by read. The fixture crosses the 65536-byte hash buffer boundary. Workspace::open reads all fixture bytes; the counter is reset before files(). The same test verifies that changes() reads all bytes and detects a same-length edit.
negative_control.original_failure: assertion left == right failed: left 131073, right 0 at the files() byte-count assertion

before.caveat: Offline warm-cache observations on one machine; no cache eviction, percentile guarantees, provider inference, or model-quality claims. Workspace open and hash verification occur before enumeration timing. Metadata and synthetic fixtures use a temporary directory that is removed on exit.

fixtures.fixture: 64 MiB regular file plus required artifact

limitations: Five warm-cache observations per fixture and variant on one macOS ARM64 machine; baseline ran before candidate, without cache eviction or randomized scheduling. Concurrent host activity was not controlled.
No provider inference or credentials were read. These measurements establish filesystem work and path equivalence, not prompt-token or model-quality effects.
The byte-read counter covers the real regular-file fingerprint read path. It is omitted outside cfg(test).

This filesystem rejected non-UTF8 fixture creation with OS error 92, so the shared filename validator is tested on constructed invalid paths. Unix symlink and socket fixtures ran on this host; other platforms were not executed.
